title: ByteWolf Speech Transcript v0.1
description: One recognised utterance, as the speech adapter publishes it to the Cognitive Runtime. Speech is an input, never an authority: a transcript may carry at most a command_suggestion, which still travels draft_flight_request -> reviewed MissionSpec -> SafetyGate -> explicit approval. There is deliberately no field for a structured command, mission or actuator, so a spoken instruction cannot be expressed as an executable one. Raw audio never enters the contract. See docs/speech-adapter-v0_1.md.

contract_version.description: Pins the meaning of every field below. A consumer that does not know this version rejects the transcript rather than guess.

transcript_id.description: Unique id for this utterance, so a suggestion can be correlated with the turn and the audit record it produced.

source.description: Where the audio came from, e.g. 'mic:headset' or 'telegram:voice'. Free text for audit, never for dispatch.

session_id.description: Optional opaque conversation key. A local development identity boundary, not authentication.

observed_at.description: RFC 3339, UTC, with an explicit offset. When the utterance was spoken -- age is measured from here, so a slow recogniser cannot pass an old instruction off as current.

max_age_s.description: How long this transcript stays usable after observed_at. A spoken request that has aged out must not be acted on: the situation it referred to may be gone.

validity.description: What the recogniser knows. 'valid': it trusts the text. 'invalid': it heard audio but does not trust the result. 'missing': no speech was recognised. 'stale' is not declared here; only the consumer knows the current time.

engine.description: Which recogniser produced this, so a regression is attributable and a consumer can pin.

language.description: BCP-47 language tag of the recognised speech, e.g. 'hu-HU'. Recorded because a wrong-language transcription is a common and quiet failure.

language_confidence.description: How sure the recogniser is about the language, when it detects rather than is told.

text.description: The recognised words. May be empty when validity is 'missing'; an empty string is not silence-means-yes, it is nothing to act on.

confidence.description: The recogniser's confidence in the text.

is_final.description: Whether this is the settled transcript rather than a streaming partial. A partial may never carry a command_suggestion.

audio_ref.description: Opaque reference to locally retained audio evidence. The contract never carries the audio itself.

command_suggestion.description: At most a suggestion that the user asked for something actionable. It is free text plus a confidence -- never a structured command, mission, waypoint or actuator instruction -- and it changes nothing on its own.

intent_text.description: What the user appears to have asked for, in their own words. The Cognitive Runtime decides what, if anything, to draft from it.

requires_approval.description: Always true. A spoken request cannot be self-approving: it still goes through reviewed MissionSpec, the SafetyGate and an explicit human approval. A document claiming otherwise is invalid by this contract, so the boundary is enforced by the schema rather than by convention.

then.description: Only a settled transcript may suggest anything: a streaming partial is still changing, and acting on half an utterance is how 'ne szállj fel' becomes 'szállj fel'.
